newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LAWLESS PENALTIES GIVE NATAL 29-24 WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LAWLESS PENALTIES GIVE NATAL 29-24 WIN.

text.p: Two penalties in the final three minutes by full-back Gavin Lawless gave Natal a hard-fought 29-24 victory over Wellington in their Super 12 match on Friday.
Natal's fourth win in the competition took them level with Auckland and Gauteng in second place in the Super 12 standings on 20 points. Australian Capital Territory top the table.
The Natal Sharks, outscored by three tries to two, had to dig deep in a bruising encounter to prevent the New Zealanders collecting a third successive win in South Africa.
Despite conceding the advantage in both territory and possession during the first half, Wellington led 14-9 at the break.
Lawless, who was successful with seven kicks out of eight for 19 points, landed three penalties to give the home team a 9-0 lead.

But twice within three minutes Natal squandered golden try-scoring opportunities -- a forward pass to left wing Cabous van der Westhuizen with the line beckoning and a knock-on by centre Geoff Appleford right in front of the posts.
Against the run of play, Wellington reduced the deficit to 9-7 when fly-half Stephen Bachop scored a try and on the stroke of halftime hooker Norm Hewitt went over in the right corner.
Six minutes into the second half Appleford scored a try which Lawless converted to give Natal a 16-14 lead.

A slicing, diagonal run from inspirational Wellington full-back Christian Cullen set up a try for right wing Tana Umaga in the 52nd minute but Natal responded with a penalty try soon afterwards when Cullen obstructed Lawless who had chipped ahead with the line in sight.
A Jon Preston penalty in the 65th minute gave Wellington a one-point lead but the reliable boot of Lawless punished Wellington indiscipline and finally won it for Natal.

Natal - Gavin Lawless; Joos Joubert, Jeremy Thomson, Geoff Appleford, Cabous van der Westhuizen; Henry Honiball (Jaco van der Westhuyzen 53) , Kevin Putt; Gary Teichmann (captain), Wayne Fyvie, Wickus van Heerden (Dieter Kriese 67), Mark Andrews John Slade, Adrian Garvey, John Allan, Ollie le Roux (Rob Kempson 69).

Wellington - Christian Cullen; Tana Umaga (Mark Ranby 74), Alama Ieremia, Jason O'Halloran, Roger Randle; Stephen Bachop, Jon Preston; Karl Williams, Martin Leslie, Chresten Davis, Mark Cooksley, Dion Waller (Filo Tiatia 63), Phil Coffin, Norm Hewitt, Mark Allen.
